extraction_notes:
WHAT WAS FETCHED, AND HOW THE TWO EXTRACTION HAZARDS WERE GUARDED AGAINST.

RETRIEVAL. Google Patents returned HTTP 503 on essentially every request for
US 10,927,377 B2 across ~10 attempts spread over 20+ minutes. The working route was
FreePatentsOnline (https://www.freepatentsonline.com/<number>.html), which serves a
direct rendering of the USPTO grant full-text XML: the pages carry the USPTO DTD
elements themselves (<patent-tables>, <table>, p-id/num attributes), so table row and
column structure - including colspan - is preserved rather than flattened. All tables
were parsed from that markup, never from flattened text and never from rendered pixels.
For US 10,100,310 B2 Google Patents did eventually respond, and its rendering of the
platelet table (Table 54) matched the FreePatentsOnline extraction CELL FOR CELL across
all 10 rows x 6 columns. That cross-check validates the whole pipeline. US 10,927,377 B2
could not be cross-checked against a second host (Google Patents 503; patentguru HTTP
468; Espacenet 403), so its rows rest on a single transcription - flagged here honestly,
though the internal consistency evidence below is strong.

HAZARD 1 - LINE-WRAPPED SEQUENCE CELLS. This is not hypothetical: Table 50 of the PKK
patent, which is the very table that lists the nine compounds dosed in the cynomolgus
study, has EVERY sequence cell wrapped across two table rows. A naive [ACGT]-run regex
over Table 50 returns 8-mers and 10-mers (e.g. ISIS 546232 -> "AGGAACTTGG" instead of
AGGAACTTGGTGTGCCACTT). Guard applied: no sequence was accepted from Table 50 at all.
Every PKK sequence was taken from the UNWRAPPED entry in an earlier table (Tables 7-24)
and accepted only where its length equalled the independently declared target
start/stop span (stop - start + 1). All nine passed: seven 20-mers and two 16-mers. Two
of the nine (ISIS 546254, ISIS 546343) are additionally characterised verbatim in the
patent's prose ("...having a sequence of (from 5' to 3') TGCAAGTCTCTTGGCAAACA..."), and
both prose sequences match the de-wrapped table cells exactly - an end-to-end check that
the de-wrapping rule is right. Declared motif length is a third check: "5-10-5 MOE" = 20
and "eekd10kke" = 3+10+3 = 16, both matching.

For the APOL1 patent, 2,631 sequence rows were extracted across 38 design tables under a
rule that accepted a sequence ONLY if its length matched at least one independent
declaration - the target start/stop span, the sugar-motif sum, or both. 1,899 rows
validated on the target span and 732 more on the motif sum; ZERO rows failed both, and
zero conflicts arose (no compound number ever mapped to two different sequences across
tables). All 2,579 distinct compounds are 16-mers, consistent with the patent's own
statement that these are 16-nucleoside gapmers, and with claim 2. An early buggy version
of the motif-sum function treated "d10" as 11 nucleosides and rejected 732 correct rows;
the patent's own legend ("the number after 'd' indicates the number of deoxy
nucleosides") settled it. That bug is exactly the failure mode the brief warns about,
caught by the validator rather than by eye.

HAZARD 1b - HEADER/DATA COLUMN MISALIGNMENT (a third silent mis-parse, found and fixed
during verification). In Tables 103 and 54 (both cynomolgus platelet tables) and Table 74
(the mouse table), the patent's header row OMITS the leading row-label cell, so the header
is one cell shorter than the data rows. Indexing the data row by hdr.index('Platelets')
therefore reads the column to the LEFT of the intended one - it silently returned the RBC
count (e.g. 6.0 x10^6/uL) in place of the platelet count (440 x10^3/uL), a plausible-looking
number in the wrong units. The first build of this lane contained that error in 35 of its
55 patent rows. It was caught by a post-hoc check that re-derived every value from the raw
HTML rather than trusting the builder. Fixes now in place: headers are RIGHT-ALIGNED against
the data rows (offset = ncol_data - ncol_header); the selected column's entry in the units
row must equal the expected unit string as printed ("(x103/uL)" or "(K/uL)"); and the
control value must exceed 100, which no single-digit RBC count can. All three assertions
fire at build time. Every one of the 55 patent platelet values, its cited control value and
its assigned grade were then re-verified against an independent transcription of the five
tables - 55/55 match - and the nine PKK values were additionally confirmed cell-for-cell
against the Google Patents rendering.

HAZARD 2 - CASE / COLOUR ENCODING OF CHEMISTRY. Neither patent encodes chemistry by
letter case, font colour or underline. Both state the encoding explicitly in running
text, which is what was used. APOL1 patent: "'k' means cEt sugar; 'e' means 2'-MOE
sugar; 'd' means deoxy sugar, and the number after 'd' indicates the number of deoxy
nucleosides", plus "The internucleoside linkages throughout each gapmer are
phosphorothioate (P=S) linkages" and "All cytosine residues ... are 5-methylcytosines".
PKK patent: the same for 5-10-5 MOE gapmers and for the "eekd10kke" deoxy/MOE/cEt
motifs. backbone_chemistry=full_PS and ps_count=length-1 therefore come from the text
layer, not from a rendering. Where the text layer could not carry an encoding, TBD was
used: ISIS 3521 has no stated sugar chemistry, and avacincaptad pegol's backbone was set
to full_PO / ps_count 0 only because the systematic chemical name printed in the FDA
review is a hydrogen PHOSPHATE ester with no thioate declared anywhere in the document.

ONE COMPOUND LEFT DELIBERATELY INCOMPLETE. Table 74 of the APOL1 patent lists a compound
"696162" that appears nowhere else in the patent. Table 87 of the same patent lists
"969162", which does have a sequence. It is almost certainly a digit transposition in
the patent itself, but the sequence is NOT asserted: ISIS 696162 carries its measured
mouse platelet count with sequence, length and ps_count all TBD, and the note explains
why. Merging it into ISIS 969162 would have been a guess.

GRADING OF ANIMAL PLATELET COUNTS. Mouse (~1150 K/uL), rat (~700 K/uL) and cynomolgus
(~380-460 x10^3/uL) baselines are not comparable to the human CTCAE thresholds the
rubric is written against, so every animal row is graded on the count RELATIVE TO THE
CONCURRENT CONTROL GROUP IN THE SAME TABLE: ratio >= 0.80 -> grade 0; 0.55-0.79 ->
grade 1; 0.20-0.54 -> grade 2; < 0.20 -> grade 3. The bands are anchored so they map
onto the rubric's human cut-offs if the control mean is treated as a normal human count
of 275 x10^9/L (midpoint of 150-400): 0.55 x 275 = 151, i.e. the lower limit of normal;
0.20 x 275 = 55, i.e. the <50 x10^9/L severe boundary. The grade-0 band at <=20% change
reflects n=4 group sizes and matches both patents' own assessment that these values were
"within the expected range for antisense oligonucleotides". Each measurement note
carries the exact percent-of-control so any downstream re-grading is trivial.

WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED. Table 83 of the PKK patent reports reduced platelet
aggregation in a FeCl3-induced mesenteric thrombus model after ISIS 482584. That is
ON-TARGET antithrombotic pharmacology - inhibiting prekallikrein is meant to reduce
thrombus formation - so it is intended mechanism, not toxicity, and no row was created.
The same line was drawn for aptamers: anti-vWF (ARC1779), anti-thrombin and anti-factor
IXa (pegnivacogin/REG1) aptamers inhibit platelet function BY DESIGN and were excluded
on that basis. The aptamer rows that ARE included come from avacincaptad pegol, an
anti-C5 aptamer with no intended platelet pharmacology whatsoever, so its
thrombocytopenia in high-dose systemic toxicology is unambiguously an unintended effect.
Its platelet INCREASE in the monkey range-finding study is recorded as grade 0 with
effect_direction "increase", since thrombocytosis is not the endpoint being graded.

WHAT COULD NOT BE GOT. (1) Pegaptanib remains a genuine gap and this lane closed rather
than filled it: the EMA Macugen scientific discussion (39 pp) and product information
(29 pp) were both fetched and contain ZERO occurrences of platelet, thrombocyt or
haematology, and pegaptanib has no openFDA label record. That is an absence of
reporting, not an explicit no-effect finding, so no grade-0 row was created from it.
(2) REG1/pegnivacogin/RB006/RB007 and ARC1779: no open-access primary source with
platelet data was located; REGULATE-PCI (PMID 26547100) has no PMC record. Recorded as
leads. (3) Neither patent contains ex-vivo aggregometry, so the aggregometry half of
Task 1 has no data to extract - the platelet data in both is absolute counts only.
(4) Frazier 2015 attributes a quotation about transient thrombocytopenia in an
anticancer trial to "Cuddihy et al. 1999", but the Cuddihy 1999 entry in that review's
own reference list is a PKR/p53 paper in Mol Cell Biol - an evident mis-citation in the
review. No row was created from it. (5) Frazier's anti-BCL2 dose-limiting
thrombocytopenia (Waters 2000) is real but the review prints no compound code, so no
defensible join key exists; the row was dropped rather than invented, and the primary
paper is listed in sources_found. (6) bepirovirsen's 80/229 count is a SECOND-HAND
report inside the meta-analysis; the Yuen 2022 NEJM primary paper was not fetched.
(7) The Figure S2 chemistry subgroup effect sizes exist only as forest-plot diamonds
with no printed numbers, so those two rows carry readout_value TBD and only the
direction/significance the text states.

REFERENCE MINING (Task 2). The meta-analysis reference list yielded five primary
mechanistic platelet papers not previously covered - Slingsby 2022 Haematologica
(2'-MOE ASOs activate human platelets via GPVI), Valenzuela 2023 Pharmaceutics (minipig
ASO platelet activation, CC BY), Sewing 2017 PLoS One (in-vitro risk factors for
oligonucleotide thrombocytopenia, CC BY - the highest-value target found), Flierl 2015
J Exp Med (PS backbone as a potent platelet activator), Zaslavsky 2021 Thromb Res - plus
two clinical papers the meta-analysis singles out for unusually good platelet reporting:
Oral 2022 (BROADEN/volanesorsen, which contains a separate table of platelet reduction
counts even where they did not reach thrombocytopenia) and Brannagan 2022 (inotersen
NEURO-TTR OLE, reporting missed doses due to platelet monitoring). All are in
sources_found with expected row counts.

CONTROLLED CONTRASTS WORTH KNOWING ABOUT. The APOL1 patent turned out to be a chemistry
matrix, not just a compound list: the same nucleobase sequence recurs under different
sugar motifs. SEQ ID NO 413 (GTATTTCTTGATGTGG) appears as ISIS 969162 (kek-d9-eekk),
ISIS 969210 (kk-d10-keke) and ISIS 969433 (kk-d9-ekeke) - and all three are the most
thrombocytopenic compounds in rat Table 87 (144, 294 and 112 K/uL against a 725 K/uL
PBS control), while ISIS 969210 and ISIS 969433 - together with the probable-typo ISIS 696162, which
carries the same target region - sit at 80-92% of control in mouse Table 74. That is
a sequence-driven, species-discordant platelet effect held constant across three
distinct wing chemistries. SEQ ID NO 1925 (CGTCAATATATTCTTT) gives a cleaner one-variable
pair: ISIS 972163 (kkk-d9-kkke) 556 K/uL versus ISIS 972116 (kkk-d9-keke) 325 K/uL in
the same rat table - identical bases, identical gap, one wing nucleoside changed from
cEt to MOE, and a 41% difference in platelet count. SEQ ID NO 1577 (CAGTTTTGTAAGTGCA)
spans ISIS 969160, 969502 and 972002, and SEQ ID NO 1904 (TATTTCTTGATGTGGT) spans ISIS
969408 and 971925. In the PKK patent, ISIS 547457 (AAGGCGATATCATGATTCCC, 5-10-5 MOE) and
ISIS 548048 (CGATATCATGATTCCC, eek-d10-kke) are a 20-mer and its own 3'-terminal 16-mer
against the same hotspot - a length-plus-chemistry pair at matched dose. Finally, ISIS
972163 and ISIS 972190 each carry counts in all three species in the APOL1 patent
(mouse, rat and cynomolgus) at documented doses, which makes them usable as
cross-species anchors.
